quote: internal static function decryptByteArray(source:ByteArray, key:int) : ByteArray { ... for(var i:int = 3; i < 256; i++) { if(i % 11 == 0) { temp = int(ba[i]); ba[i] = ba[i + 256]; ba[i + 256] = temp; } ba[i] ^= key; } ... }  ·  resourceFileNameArray:Array = ["shs3resource.swf","musicresource.swf","soundresource.swf","imageresource.swf","bgresource.swf"]  =>  keys h=104 u=117 o=111 m=109 g=103
text: The audio is RECOVERED, not encrypted-beyond-reach. The game's own decryptor is in the repo: ResourceManager.decryptByteArray XORs bytes 3..255 with key = resourceFileNameArray[num].charCodeAt(1) AND swaps ba[i] with ba[i+256] whenever i%11==0. Applying it to all five Mobile_*Resource.bin files yields valid SWFs. 122_Mobile_SoundResource inflates to 29,623 bytes holding 13 DefineSound tags (deflect, die1, die2, die3, slash1, slash2, slash3, punch, hitmetal, fart, goodkoto, sumo, refund) and 113_Mobile_MusicResource inflates to 1,402,677 bytes holding 13 DefineSound music stems (bgm_lose, safepercussion, safekoto, safeambience, bgm_levelup, bgm_gangnam, flutes, dungeonpiano, dungeonpercussion, dungeonflute, dungeonambience, battledrums, battlechants) — all MP3, 11025 Hz, 16-bit, mono. These are byte-exact original assets, not characterisations from a YouTube rip. A plain whole-file XOR fails 68 bytes into the deflate stream, which is why every prior pass concluded 'unopenable'; the i%11 byte-swap is the missing step.

lane_impact: L-combat-core: weakens (without killing) the 300/200/100-as-base arithmetic, and tells the port to derive reach from the SPD/DAN formula rather than from the 200 constant.
quote: §1t1541s0§.as:51 `internal static var maxDistance:int = 200;` · :106-108 `public static function §1t10094s0§(param1:int) : * { maxDistance = param1; }` · §1t99s0§.as:3158 `§1t1541s0§.§1t10094s0§(this.§1t4417s0§);` inside setStance · §1t1523s0§.as:2347 `return int(120 + Math.floor(_loc2_ * param1 / (20 + param1)));`
text: InputManager.maxDistance = 200 is a compile-time initialiser, not a gameplay base. setStance calls InputManager.setMaxDistance(slashLength) on every battle init for the local player (web §1t99s0§.as:3156-3158, android MCSPlayer.as:3092-3094), so the 200 is overwritten before the player ever draws a stroke. Any derivation of the wiki's 300/200/100 that treats 200 as 'the shipped default slash budget' rests on a value the player never plays at. The real base is 120 + floor((90 + 5*DAN) * SPD / (20 + SPD)) — 124 at SPD 1 / dan 0, asymptotically 210 at dan 0.

text: EVERY 'stage px' NUMBER IN docs/research/fidelity/COMBAT_MEASUREMENTS.md THAT WAS CONVERTED AT /1.875 IS 20% TOO LARGE. The correct 1080p divisor is 2.25. The web build's letterbox routine sets base 800x480 and, for a viewport wider than 800/480 = 1.6667, takes the fit-height branch: scale = stageHeight/480 and offsetX = (stageWidth - 800*scale)/2. At 1920x1080 that is scale 2.25 with 60 px pillarbox bars. Three independent confirmations: (1) source, §1t1540s0§.as:271-307 plus §1t1523s0§.as:104/106 (stageWidth 800, stageHeight 480); (2) frames -- I measured the pillarbox on four session11 frames (first/last column with any pixel >12): damage-ttk/t125.350.png 54->1862, gap-focus-trigger/t1747.000.png 48->1867, stance-reach/B_t783.400_LIGHT_stroke-anchored-at-body_farGap436px.png 52->1868, stance-reach/A_t117.400_BALANCED_lvl1_stroke235px.png 54->1863, i.e. content ~1810-1820 px = 800x2.25 = 1800 plus compression bleed, whereas /1.875 demands 210 px black bars that are simply not present; (3) reductio -- the HUD reload bar sits at row y=1036 (I measured it), which at /1.875 maps to stage y ~504, off the bottom of a 480-tall stage, physically impossible, while at /2.25 it maps to stage y ~460 of 480, i.e. the bottom HUD strip.
